title: When the Well Wakes
premise: Petra Nystrom, a pest controller who trusts traps over talk, is called to her late grandmother's farmhouse where something leaves greasy fingerprints at exactly chair-height and rearranges the family photographs to include an empty seat. Digging through her grandmother's ledgers, she learns that decades ago the family 'invited in' a presence to save a dying child — an invitation renewed each generation by someone who must willingly sit in the extra chair. As the house wakes around her, Petra discovers she is the last of the bloodline, and the thing at the table has been waiting for her name. To end it, she must choose between loyalty to the family's long bargain and the truth her grandmother hid: the presence can be uninvited, but only by someone willing to give up every memory of belonging.
about_author: S. M. Underhill grew up in rural Minnesota, where farmhouses outnumber streetlights and every old family keeps one story it never tells twice. A former building inspector, they write horror about houses that remember more than the people inside them.

chapters.title: The Call Comes at Dusk
chapters.summary: POV Petra. A pest-control job on her dead grandmother's road — a house she hasn't entered since the funeral. She takes it out of stubbornness, not sentiment. Beat: dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Fingerprints at Chair-Height
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Greasy handprints ring the kitchen walls, all level with a seated person, none near doors or windows. No droppings, no tracks, no entry point. Beat: professional confidence beginning to crack.

chapters.title: Counting Doors
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Her ritual: lights on, doors counted, thresholds chalked. By morning there are eleven doors in a nine-door house. Beat: the rules she lives by stop working.

chapters.title: The Extra Chair
chapters.summary: POV Petra. In the attic photographs, every family portrait now includes a wooden chair no one sits in — including photos taken before her birth. Beat: inheritance turning sinister.

chapters.title: What the Neighbors Won't Say
chapters.summary: POV Petra. A neighbor, Alma Voss, warns her off with odd courtesy: 'Your grandmother kept her appointments.' Refuses to explain. Beat: isolation deepening; the town knows something.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Hidden in the pantry, a ledger of dates, initials, and one recurring word: RENEWED. The last entry is dated three days after the funeral — after grandma died. Beat: the past becomes a contract.

chapters.title: First Knock
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Three knocks from inside the sealed root cellar, patient as a metronome. She answers with a crowbar and finds nothing but warmth, like breath. Beat: fear becoming personal.

chapters.title: The Child Who Didn't Die
chapters.summary: POV Petra, flashback woven in. Church records reveal a sibling Petra never knew — Uncle Anders, who drowned in 1961, then didn't. The ledger begins the week he lived again. Beat: the bargain revealed.

chapters.title: Alma's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Alma. She was a girl when the Nystroms made their arrangement; her own family fled rather than take a turn sitting in the chair. She tells Petra what renewal costs. Beat: loyalty vs. truth sharpening.

chapters.title: The House Learns Her Name
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Wallpaper peels to show PETRA penciled beneath layers, in a child's hand, dated decades ago. Beat: she was always expected.

chapters.title: Doors Thirteen and Fourteen
chapters.summary: POV Petra. New doors appear overnight, both locked, both warm. Behind one, faintly, her grandmother's voice humming a lullaby. Beat: grief weaponized.

chapters.title: The Chair Arrives
chapters.summary: POV Petra. The wooden chair from the photographs stands in the kitchen, real, dusted, pulled slightly from the table as if for a guest. Beat: the trap closing gently.

chapters.title: Rules of Invitation
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Researching folklore, she maps the mechanics: invited things can't be forced out, only uninvited — and uninvitation requires the inviter's blood to renounce the welcome aloud. Beat: hope with a price tag.

chapters.title: A Night of Small Courtesies
chapters.summary: POV Petra. The presence tidies for her: dishes washed, fire laid, her boots dried. It wants to be a good host's guest. Beat: horror softening into terrible intimacy.

chapters.title: Anders in the Glass
chapters.summary: POV Petra. A mirror shows a drowned boy standing behind her, smiling, unchanged since 1961. He signs thank you in the fogged glass. Beat: pity entangling fear.

chapters.title: Alma Disappears
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Alma's porch light burns with no one home; her door count is wrong too. The house is collecting witnesses. Beat: stakes turn lethal.

chapters.title: The Renewal Clause
chapters.summary: POV Petra. The ledger's final pages decode: if no heir renews the invitation by the next new moon, the presence collects what it was owed instead — a life per missed generation. Beat: clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Last Tape
chapters.summary: POV Petra. A cassette labeled FOR THE ONE WHO COUNTS DOORS. Grandma admits she meant to break the chain and failed, and begs Petra not to sit down. Beat: posthumous love, posthumous guilt.

chapters.title: The Lullaby Trap
chapters.summary: POV Petra. The house sings the lullaby in her mother's voice, then her own. She nearly follows it to chair thirteen before her chalk lines hold. Beat: temptation nearly wins.

chapters.title: Halfway Point: The Table Is Set
chapters.summary: POV Petra. She wakes to find dinner laid for two, her place marked with her grandmother's brooch. The fingerprints are fresh on the back of her chair. Beat: midpoint — the choice is no longer abstract.

chapters.title: What Was Invited
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Piecing together records, she learns the presence isn't a demon but something older and hungrier — a tenant spirit the family mistook for a miracle. Beat: the truth reframes everything.

chapters.title: Mother's Phone Call
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Her estranged mother calls, oddly calm, urging her to 'just sit, sweetheart, it's easier.' The call traces to the farmhouse landline, unplugged. Beat: betrayal inside the bloodline.

chapters.title: Chalk and Iron
chapters.summary: POV Petra. She fortifies: iron filings, salt, chalked thresholds, every light burning. The house responds politely by adding windows. Beat: resistance meeting adaptation.

chapters.title: Alma Found
chapters.summary: POV Petra. She finds Alma seated at her own kitchen table, entranced, an extra chair across from her. Petra breaks the trance by speaking Alma's true name aloud. Beat: first victory; method discovered.

chapters.title: Names Have Weight
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Naming worked because the presence trades in identity. To uninvite it, she must speak its true name — which the ledger hides in plain sight. Beat: puzzle tightening.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Cipher
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Dates in the ledger map to hymn numbers; the initials spell a name in the church's founding register: VESSEL-WARDEN, the thing the town itself first invited. Beat: complicity widens beyond the family.

chapters.title: Town Meeting Nobody Called
chapters.summary: POV Petra. At the grange hall, townsfolk urge renewal — several bear fingerprint bruises at chair-height. The whole valley has been paying interest for a century. Beat: belonging revealed as hostage-taking.

chapters.title: They Want Her Seated
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Neighbors carry her toward the farmhouse 'for her own good.' She escapes through a door that wasn't there yesterday, into the fields. Beat: loyalty vs. truth turns physical.

chapters.title: Night in the Corn
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Hunted through frozen cornrows by polite footsteps, she survives by counting — doors, rows, breaths — until dawn scatters them. Beat: endurance; her rituals become armor.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Grave
chapters.summary: POV Petra. At the grave, fresh flowers and a chair-shaped patch of dead grass. Grandma's headstone bears the same initials as the ledger's first entry. Beat: grief and rage fusing into resolve.

chapters.title: The Second Tape
chapters.summary: POV Petra. A tape hidden in the coffin vault reveals the uninvitation rite — and that it erases every memory the speaker holds of the family. Grandma couldn't bear to forget. Beat: the full price named.

chapters.title: New Moon Eve
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Deadline tomorrow. The house goes gentle: warm bread, folded laundry, Anders weeping in mirrors, begging her to stay. Beat: the cruelest temptation yet.

chapters.title: She Almost Sits
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Exhausted, grieving, she lowers herself toward the chair — and stops at the feel of grandma's brooch in her pocket, cold as a verdict. Beat: nadir and pivot.

chapters.title: Unplugging the House
chapters.summary: POV Petra. She cuts power, water, every line feeding the farm. The lights stay on anyway. 'I keep the lights on,' she says. 'Not you.' Beat: reclaiming her own creed.

chapters.title: The Warden Speaks
chapters.summary: POV Petra. The presence finally shows itself — courteous, ancient, wearing the faces of everyone who ever fed it. It offers her Anders, alive, forever, for one sitting. Beat: climax pressure peak.

chapters.title: The Uninvitation
chapters.summary: POV Petra. At the table before witnesses' marks, she speaks the Warden's true name and renounces the invitation in the family's voice, generations thick. The house screams politely. Beat: climax.

chapters.title: What It Costs
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Memories burn away as she speaks — grandma's face, the funeral, the lullaby — until she stands in a silent kitchen unable to say why she's crying. Beat: victory hollowed by loss.

chapters.title: Eleven Doors Again
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Morning. Nine doors, eleven counted out of habit. The chair is kindling; the photographs show only family. Anders's photo remains, finally just a drowned boy. Beat: release.

chapters.title: Alma Remembers For Her
chapters.summary: POV Alma. Alma returns the memories Petra lost, told over coffee: who she was, whom she loved, what she paid. Belonging rebuilt by witness instead of blood. Beat: theme resolved — chosen loyalty.

chapters.title: Sunrise Appointment
chapters.summary: POV Petra. She keeps the pest-control appointment anyway, walks the empty house, and leaves the lights off for the first time. On the doorstep, a business card: another house, another call. Beat: quiet ending; the work continues.
